articles.title: Cyclone Arnab on the way? Deep depression lashes Odisha, forces school closures and evacuation prep in 11 - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Cyclone Arnab on the way? Deep depression lashes Odisha, forces school closures and evacuation prep in 11 districts; red alert issued
It is expected to move west-northwestwards and intensify into a deep depression over the next 12 hours.
The system is likely to cross the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coasts between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur during the night of September 23 and early hours of September 24.
IMD has warned of heavy to very heavy rainfall in southern and coastal Odisha, with isolated extremely heavy rain in some areas.
Odisha shuts schools as rain lashes state
Heavy rain triggered by the depression lashed coastal and southern Odisha on Tuesday, prompting district administrations to shut schools and anganwadi centres in several areas.Schools were closed for the day in Khurda, Jagatsinghpur, Ganjam and Gajapati, while Malkangiri ordered schools to remain closed till September 24. Anganwadi centres will also remain closed in the affected areas.
The National Rural Talent Scholarship examination scheduled for Tuesday will be held as planned at designated centres.
11 Odisha districts on high alert
Odisha chief secretary Anu Garg said collectors of 11 districts had been put on high alert following the IMD warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall in the southern and coastal parts of the state.Authorities have kept cyclone and flood shelters ready and are preparing for possible waterlogging, urban flooding, landslides and mudslides.
Government employees' leave has also been cancelled in Ganjam, Koraput and Kalahandi, while teachers in Koraput and Kalahandi have been directed not to leave their places of posting until September 25.
Vehicular movement has been restricted on some roads, including Kalinga Ghat between Ganjam and Kandhamal. Ferry services between Satapada and Jahnikuda in Chilika Lake will remain suspended until September 25.
Red alert for southern Odisha
IMD has issued a red alert for parts of southern Odisha from September 23 to 25. Koraput, Gajapati and Ganjam are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rain, with extremely heavy rain at isolated places, on September 23 and 24.Kalahandi, Nabarangpur, Koraput and Malkangiri are under red alert for September 24 and 25. Rainfall is expected to continue in parts of the state until September 25.
Squalls with winds gusting up to 75 kmph are also likely along and off the south Odisha-north Andhra Pradesh coasts from the morning of September 23 to the evening of September 24.
So, what is Cyclone Arnab?
Arnab is not the name of the current depression. It is the next unused name in the predetermined list of tropical cyclone names for the North Indian Ocean.The list is maintained under the WMO/ESCAP Panel on tropical cyclones, with names contributed by member countries.
Arnab was contributed by Bangladesh and appears in the roster after the names already used in the current sequence.
A system gets a cyclone name only after reaching the required intensity. So, if a future system reaches tropical-cyclone intensity and Arnab is next in sequence, it will be called Cyclone Arnab.
For the present Odisha system, IMD has said it is expected to become a deep depression rather than a cyclone.

articles.title: Govt plans to reintroduce rhinos in VTR, may bring them from Assam & Bengal - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Govt plans to reintroduce rhinos in VTR, may bring them from Assam & Bengal
He said the department had already assessed the potential for rhinoceros conservation in VTR and was working towards launching a dedicated rehabilitation and conservation programme there. A separate plan had also been prepared to bring rhinoceros to Rajgir Zoo Safari and develop conservation facilities for them.
The minister also highlighted Patna Zoo’s contribution to rhino conservation, saying 34 rhinos had lived at the zoo over the past 38 years and 25 calves had been born there. He said the zoo’s position at the top in India in terms of the number of rhinos reflected the sustained efforts of its animal keepers and veterinarians.
The minister felicitated the animal husbandry workers, veterinary officers and experts associated with the zoo’s rhino health management.
In his address, principal chief conservator of forests (HoFF) Arvinder Singh highlighted the ecological role of rhinoceros. The department is now working on plans to identify suitable rhinoceros from Patna Zoo for relocation to VTR. Officials said the proposed move would mark a new direction for rhinoceros conservation in Bihar rather than being limited to an animal relocation exercise.
Additional principal chief conservator of forests-cum-chief wildlife warden Abhay Kumar, in his welcome address, outlined Bihar’s rhinoceros conservation efforts and the history of breeding at Patna Zoo. He said strengthening rhinoceros conservation in VTR and Rajgir Zoo Safari was the next important step for the state’s biodiversity and wildlife conservation.

articles.title: Four teachers for nine children, six for 301: Education dept’s odd arithmetic - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Four teachers for nine children, six for 301: Education dept’s odd arithmetic
A teacher said the lack of furniture was especially concerning for students in classes VI to VIII. “It may still appear manageable when younger children sit on the floor, but seeing older students, particularly girls, study in such conditions is not appropriate,” she said.
The school also has three old rooms in a dilapidated condition with fears they could collapse. Headmaster Jaivansh Ram said the school management had repeatedly informed senior education officials in writing about the damaged rooms, shortage of teachers and inadequate benches and desks, but no concrete action had been taken.
Kargahar block education officer Manoj Kumar Ram said officials had been informed about the shortage of benches and desks and the dilapidated rooms. On the shortage of subject teachers, he said appointments were made by the education department.
The contrast is sharper in Kaimur. Dubouli has four teachers for 18 students — nine boys and nine girls — in a two-storey building. All 18 students stayed away from school on Tuesday alleging that headmaster Santosh Kumar made them collect dry wood for cooking the midday meal, fetch water and clean classrooms and the school premises instead of focusing on studies. Parents alleged he remained occupied with his cellphone, while children faced confiscation of schoolbags and, in some cases, physical assault if they refused. They further alleged rice meant for the midday meal was being sold.
Santosh said the matter had been reported to the midday meal incharge and BDO-cum-incharge block education officer Ritu Ranjan Kumar. The BDO said the administration would investigate why the students stayed away and ascertain the facts behind the allegations. He said officials would meet the parents and appeal to them to send their children back to school. “If a written complaint is submitted, appropriate action will be taken after an inquiry,” Kumar said.

articles.title: Motorcycle-borne youth attacks two girls with blade in Muzaffarpur - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Motorcycle-borne youth attacks two girls with blade in Muzaffarpur
According to the SDPO, the girls were cycling to school when an unidentified motorcycle-borne youth attacked them with a blade before fleeing from the spot. One girl sustained an injury near her arm, while the other was injured around her shoulder, she said.
The injured students were taken to a primary health centre (PHC) with police assistance. Doctors provided them with treatment and said they were out of danger. They were subsequently discharged and allowed to return home, police said.
The SDPO said a case was registered on Monday against the unidentified attacker on the basis of complaints lodged by the families. Investigators are now examining CCTV footage from the area to establish the sequence of events and identify the suspect.
Technical evidence is also being analysed to track the accused, police said, adding that efforts were underway to arrest him.
The SDPO clarified that reports alleging that the girls had been molested were not supported by their statements. She also said legal notices would be issued to those allegedly responsible for spreading false information.

articles.title: ABVP activists take out protest march in Jamui, demand action in molestation incident - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Patna: Protests over the alleged molestation and assault of a minor schoolgirl in Jamui and circulation of a video of the incident were held in Jamui and Patna on Tuesday with student and opposition outfits demanding accountability, stronger security for girls and action against those involved.
In Jamui,
ABVP, the student wing of the
BJP, took out a march through major roads and intersections. The protesters demanded a detailed probe to identify everyone involved in the incident and circulation of the video, while stressing that the minor’s identity and privacy must be protected.
ABVP student Rita Kumari sought increased police patrolling around schools, colleges and coaching centres, particularly on routes used by students during morning and evening hours. Another protester, Babita Kumari, called for preventive policing and identification of vulnerable stretches.
In Patna, Youth Congress workers led by Bittu Yadav staged a demonstration at Kargil Chowk, demanding CM Samrat Choudhary’s resignation.
NSUI activists joined the protest, carrying posters with slogans including “Unsafe Streets, Silent System” and “Protect Women From BJP-RSS”.
Reminding Samrat of his earlier statement on women’s safety, Yadav said, “Now, following the Jamui incident, the people of Bihar are asking — when will that morning arrive, and when will Samrat Choudhary resign?”
Members of the Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI), the youth wing of the CPI(M), also marched and burnt the CM’s effigy near Patna Junction.
They alleged deterioration in law and order and raised concerns over the safety of schoolgirls.
The All India Democratic Women’s Association (AIDWA) demanded strict action against all accused under the POCSO Act, speedy trials, security and adequate compensation for the victim, and stronger directions to the police administration.
The outfits said they would continue raising the issue until action was taken and security arrangements for girls were strengthened.

articles.title: Sahil Wakode death: IIT-Bombay alumni body condemns ‘media trials’, seeks fair, speedy probe - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Sahil Wakode death: IIT-Bombay alumni body condemns ‘media trials’, seeks fair, speedy probe
In the statement, the alumni body said it was deeply saddened by the student's death and extended its condolences to his family.
It said the IIT-Bombay community was going through an 'immensely difficult period' and stressed the need for an equitable, inclusive, safe and supportive environment for the well-being of students, faculty and staff.
While acknowledging the responsibility of the institute's faculty and administration to uphold institutional protocols and academic standards, IITBAA called for a fair, transparent and speedy investigation into the incident.
“Empathy, fairness, and truth must guide our community forward,” the association said, adding that it remained committed to supporting students and faculty and would collaborate with the institute to strengthen mental health resources, campus well-being and trust within the community.

articles.title: Cooch Behar to develop into religious tourism hotspot: Suvendu - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
Cooch Behar to develop into religious tourism hotspot: Suvendu
Linking the airport initiative with a broader tourism push, the CM said Cooch Behar had considerable potential for religious as well as eco-tourism. He referred to Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma’s recent visit to Madhupur Dham and his own visit to the Madanmohan temple to highlight Cooch Behar’s religious significance.
“Our objective is to develop the district as a major tourism destination comparable to established north Bengal attractions such as Tiger Hill and the Dooars,” he said.
Saying there would be no shortage of funds for Cooch Behar’s overall transformation, Adhikari directed officials to expand the development plan beyond the initial Rs 2-crore detailed project report and undertake a larger package of development works.
“I took oath on May 9, 2026. By May 9, 2027, all steps will be taken to fulfil the dreams of the people of Cooch Behar,” he said.
Pointing out that land identification, preparation of DPRs and the process of fund allocation for upcoming projects had already begun, Adhikari said a substantial share of the works in the first tender issued by the north Bengal development department had been earmarked for Cooch Behar.
He promised to visit Cooch Behar during the upcoming Ras Purnima celebrations.
Speaking on the new bridge on Murti, Adhikari said it had been built at a cost of Rs 19.78 crore. He added that he had given approvals for the construction of a new bridge on Kalikhola at Nagrakata.

articles.title: BJP organises workshop on PM Modi’s public life - The Times of India
articles.full_text:
BJP organises workshop on PM Modi’s public life
Addressing the gathering, Saraogi said the theatrical presentation was more than a cultural programme; it provided a creative medium to understand PM Modi’s long public life and his approach toward public service. He praised the artists for portraying different aspects of his journey with sensitivity and impact.
“PM Modi’s public life, as CM and PM, focused on service, governance and development, with an emphasis on taking welfare and development initiatives to people at the grassroots,” he said, adding that the journey also conveyed the importance of hard work, discipline and social responsibility to young people.
He added that art and culture are effective means of communicating social thoughts and values. “Programmes like this could help spread messages of service, dedication and social responsibility among people,” Saraogi said.
While the programme was moderated by BJP state secretary Kumar Raghavendra, convener of the party’s art and culture wing Varun Singh proposed a vote of thanks.
State organisation general secretary Bhikhu Bhai Dalsania, art and culture minister Pramod Chandravanshi, Kumhrar MLA Sanjay Gupta and several state office-bearers, district campaign convenors, party workers and art enthusiasts attended the event.

articles.full_text:
Son, mother foil CSP loot bid; 2 held in Palamu
However, Rohit and his mother, Sunita Devi, fought back and managed to overpower one of the robbers. The second accused was caught by local residents who rushed to the spot after hearing their cries for help. Together, they foiled the robbery and recovered the looted cash.
SDPO Lesliganj Prashant Kumar said the bravery shown by Rohit and his mother helped thwart the robbery, while swift police intervention averted a potentially serious law-and-order situation.
Police recovered the entire stolen amount, a country-made pistol, five live cartridges, a motorcycle and a mobile phone. The accused, identified as Pawan Singh (21) and Ranbeer Singh (20), residents of Tarhassi area, were arrested and booked under relevant sections of BNS and Arms Act. “Both were remanded to judicial custody on Tuesday,” said Kumar.
During interrogation, Pawan allegedly confessed to involvement in two similar robberies at CSPs in Tarhassi and Manatu police station areas over the past two months.
According to the SDPO, the duo had also stolen a motorcycle earlier on Monday and used it in the attempted robbery. The stolen bike was recovered during the operation.
